column2: You have sent out summons to all your vassals for the blót. Those who keep the gods of the north will come to see the blood flow, and those who follow the meek gods of the south will have to offer gold to be excused from the rite.
I can hardly wait!
Summoned to the blót.
Asked to pay to be excused from the blót.

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName], has summoned you and [From.GetHerHis] other vassals to a great blót. There you will give blood to the gods and see prisoners hang from the blood-tree, before a feast where you drink in their name.
I wouldn't miss it.

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName], remains trapped in [From.GetHerHis] savage northern ways, and now [From.GetSheHe] has summoned all [From.GetHerHis] vassals to a blót where [From.GetSheHe] means to hang prisoners for [From.GetHerHis] gods. Since you do not share these barbarous rites, you are expected to pay gold to be excused.
I suppose I have no choice in the matter.
[This.Religion.GetRandomGodNameCap] be my witness, I shall not pay!
Your payment is received.
Your refusal is received.

[From.GetTitledFirstName], your vassal, is stubborn in [From.GetHerHis] ways and speaks only of the greatness of [From.Religion.GetRandomGodNameCap], but [From.GetSheHe] has wisely sent you gold to be excused from the blót.

Despite having sworn you fealty, [From.GetTitledFirstName] refuses to pay to be excused from the blót! According to [From.GetFirstName], [From.Religion.GetRandomGodName] would never forgive [From.GetHerHim] for giving a single copper to such an "uncivilized" rite.
As well [From.GetSheHe] should.
This insult will not be forgotten.

The guests have arrived, and the blót begins! You gather before the hof and slaughter the beasts first. While their meat is readied for the feast, the blood is caught in a bowl and sprinkled with twigs on the idols of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] and the other gods, and on the faithful themselves. Then it is time for the blood-tree.

The blót held by [From.GetTitledFirstName] begins! You gather before the hof as the beasts are slaughtered. While their meat is readied for the feast, the blood is caught in a bowl and sprinkled with twigs on the idols of [From.Religion.GetHighGodName] and the other gods, and on you and the other faithful. Then it is time for the blood-tree.
Now for the human offering...
Let the blood flow!

Although you have been told little, the noise from outside your cell makes it clear that your captor, [From.GetTitledFirstName], is holding a blót to give blood to [From.GetHerHis] gods. The guards burst in and drag you out towards the great blood-tree before the hof, where the bodies of beasts already hang...
No! Not like this!

Your brother, [From.GetTitledFirstName], is brought up from the dungeon and led to the blood-tree. As the noose is laid around his neck, he looks at you with pleading eyes. "Don't do this, [Root.GetFirstName]. There has to be some other way..."

Your sister, [From.GetTitledFirstName], is dragged up from the dungeon and led to the blood-tree. Tears stream down her face as the guards lay the noose around her neck. "Please, [Root.GetFirstName]," she says, her voice trembling. "Don't let them do this."

The guards drag your father, [From.GetTitledFirstName], from his cell to the blood-tree and lay the noose around his neck. "My [Root.GetSonDaughter]," he croaks, looking at you. "Can't you find it in your heart to forgive me?"

Distant screaming carries from the dungeon as your guards drag out your mother, [From.GetTitledFirstName]. They bring her to the blood-tree, and as they lay the noose around her neck she looks at you with pleading eyes. "W-why would you do this to your own mother?"

The guards fetch your son, [From.GetTitledFirstName], from the dungeon and lead him to the blood-tree. The noose is laid around his neck and the rope thrown over a thick branch. Before your men haul on it, your son looks at you with tears in his eyes. "Please don't, [Root.GetFatherMother]... please don't."

Your daughter, [From.GetTitledFirstName], is pulled from the dungeon and brought to the blood-tree. As the noose is laid around her neck she gives you a desperate, piercing glare. "Is this really what you have come to, [Root.GetFatherMother]? To do this... to your own daughter?"

Your [From.GetHusbandWife], [From.GetTitledFirstName], is dragged to the blood-tree and the noose is laid around [From.GetHerHis] neck. In a last desperate effort to save [From.GetHerselfHimself], [From.GetFirstName] calls out to you. "I have always loved you, [Root.GetFirstName]... and I always will."

[From.GetTitledFirstName] is brought from the dungeon and set beneath the blood-tree. As the noose is laid around [From.GetHerHis] neck, [From.GetFirstName] cries out to you. "Don't do this, [Root.GetFirstName]! We are family, of the same blood!"

[From.GetTitledFirstName], who speaks for all who follow [From.Religion.GetHighGodName], is dragged up from your dungeon to the blood-tree. A greater offering the gods of the north have not had in an age, and every guest in the crowd knows it.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] is brought up from the dungeon in chains that take three men to carry. The dwarf says nothing at all until the noose is around [From.GetHerHis] neck. Then, quite calmly, [From.GetSheHe] tells you that your name is already written in a book in Karaz-a-Karak, and that dwarfs do not forget.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] walks to the blood-tree as if it were [From.GetHerHis] own idea, looking at your warriors, your idols and you with the same faint disgust. The elf does not beg. Your seers whisper that the gods have not tasted such old blood in many winters.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] is hauled up from the dungeon snarling and laughing at once. The greenskin bites one guard, headbutts another, and is still bellowing that it will come back and krump the lot of you when the noose goes around its thick green neck.

From deep within your dungeon the guards drag out [From.GetTitledFirstName], a scaled creature from the steaming jungles beyond the sea. As the noose is laid around [From.GetHerHis] neck, the lizard hisses something in no tongue of men and stares at you with cold, unblinking eyes.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] is brought up from the dungeon and led to the blood-tree. As the guards lay the noose around [From.GetHerHis] neck, [From.GetSheHe] screams that [From.Religion.GetHighGodName] will swallow your soul and that the Dark Gods laugh at your little idols.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] is brought up from the dungeon and led to the blood-tree. As the guards lay the noose around [From.GetHerHis] neck, [From.GetSheHe] mutters a prayer to [From.Religion.GetHighGodName]. The gods of the south have never once come north to save one of their own.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] is brought up from the dungeon and led to the blood-tree. A noose is laid around [From.GetHerHis] neck and the rope thrown over a thick branch. A small yellow pool forms at [From.GetFirstName]'s feet.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] is brought up from the dungeon and led to the blood-tree. At the sight of the dangling noose [From.GetSheHe] shoves the nearest guard aside and runs for it, but to no avail. Your men drag [From.GetHerHim] back kicking and screaming.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] is brought up from the dungeon and led to the blood-tree. Even as the noose is laid around [From.GetHerHis] neck, [From.GetFirstName] stares ahead without showing anything at all. It seems [From.GetSheHe] has made peace with [From.GetHerHis] fate.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] is brought up from the dungeon and led to the blood-tree. The moment [From.GetSheHe] spots you in the crowd [From.GetSheHe] hurls curses and spittle your way, and keeps on even as the noose is laid around [From.GetHerHis] neck. The hatred in [From.GetHerHis] eyes cannot be mistaken.
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], we give you this one!
I'm afraid not. Do it, men.
There can be no turning back now. I'm sorry.
No.
Because I can.
Do it, men.
You have left me with little choice.
Forgive me then, my love, but this is how it must be.
Yes, and that only proves my devotion to [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].
All the might of your faith cannot save you, [From.GetBestName]!
Then write this down as well.
Let us see if elf blood is as sweet as they say.
Hang it high, where the gods can see it.
Let us show you how a proper sacrifice is done.
Your Dark Gods have no hold on the blood-tree.
Your weak southern gods won't save you...
No, I can't do this to my own brother...
No... not my own sister...
I can't do this to my own father...
I... I wouldn't...
I can't do this... not to my own boy...
No, send her back... not my girl...
No, this is too much... I can't permit it.
It is true... [From.GetSheHe] is kin.
No, I have changed my mind.

Your liege has [From.GetHerHis] men fetch [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], [From.GetHerHis] own brother, from the dungeon. [From.GetFirstName] shows no feeling at all as [blot_victim.GetFirstName] is led to the blood-tree, and soon his body turns slowly in the wind.

It seems your liege means to give [From.GetHerHis] own sister, [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], to the gods. She is brought out of [From.GetFirstName]'s dungeon squinting in the daylight while the guards lay the noose around her neck. Moments later her eyes are forever dull.

To your surprise, [From.GetTitledFirstName] orders the guards to bring out [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], [From.GetHerHis] own father. He is led to the blood-tree, and soon he hangs among the beasts with dead, gaping eyes.

[blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], the mother of your liege, appears at the hof flanked by guards, and to your surprise they lead her straight to the blood-tree. She pleads with [From.GetTitledFirstName] in vain. Within moments she hangs beside the other offerings.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] marches [From.GetHerHis] own son, [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], to the blood-tree. He is to be the next offering. All his pleas fall on deaf ears, and moments later the noose is around his neck and he is silent forever.

The crowd at the blót gasps when [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], daughter of [From.GetTitledFirstName], is dragged to the blood-tree for the next offering. She begs her [From.GetFatherMother] for mercy, but none is forthcoming.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has apparently decided to give [From.GetHerHis] own spouse, [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], to the gods, and [blot_victim.GetSheHe] is brought in chains to the blood-tree. Despite all [blot_victim.GetHerHis] words of love, [From.GetFirstName] goes ahead with it.

[blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], one of [From.GetFirstName]'s own kin, is dragged from the dungeon to the blood-tree. Despite the blood they share, or perhaps because of it, [From.GetFirstName] shows no mercy.

Your liege's guards drag [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], the head of [blot_victim.Religion.GetName], to the blood-tree. The crowd roars as [blot_victim.GetSheHe] kicks [blot_victim.GetHerHis] last. A greater offering the gods of the north have not had in an age.

A dwarf, [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], is hanged from the blood-tree. It takes a long time, and the dwarf curses your liege in Khazalid until the very end. Someone mutters that the throng of the mountains will not forget this.

An elf, [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], is hanged from the blood-tree without a word of complaint. The seers say the gods have not tasted such old blood in many winters, and the crowd is strangely quiet afterwards.
A greenskin, [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], is dragged to the blood-tree biting and bellowing. It takes six men to get the noose around its neck, and the crowd cheers every one of them.

In honor of the blót your liege brings out a lizardman from the jungles beyond the sea. [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName] is hanged from the blood-tree, still staring coldly at the crowd, and all agree it is a most worthy offering.

Your liege's guards bring [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], a servant of the Dark Gods, to the blood-tree. [blot_victim.GetSheHeCap] screams that [blot_victim.Religion.GetHighGodName] will swallow all your souls right up until the rope goes tight.

Your liege's guards bring [blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName], who follows [blot_victim.Religion.GetHighGodName], to the blood-tree. As the noose is laid around [blot_victim.GetHerHis] neck, [blot_victim.GetSheHe] prattles on about how you will all burn for your sins... but soon [blot_victim.GetSheHe] says no more.

[blot_victim.GetTitledFirstName] is dragged to the blood-tree and the noose is laid around [blot_victim.GetHerHis] neck. Soon [blot_victim.GetFirstName]'s body hangs limp in the cold wind among the beasts.

As [From.GetTitledFirstName] had no prisoners in [From.GetHerHis] dungeon fit for the blót, your liege made do with a few thralls bought for the purpose. They are led to the blood-tree, and soon they hang limp from its thick branches.
This should please the gods!
Better than nothing, I suppose.

As you stand trembling with the noose around your neck, [From.GetTitledFirstName] suddenly seems to change [From.GetHerHis] mind. The noose is lifted off and you are taken back to your cell. It looks like you will live to see another day.
I... how... what?
The hanging is stayed.

You have no prisoners in your dungeon fit for the blót, so you must make do with a few thralls bought for the purpose. They are led to the blood-tree, and soon they hang limp from its thick branches. The gods will take it, but they have had better.
It is better than nothing.
With the hanging done, the feast at the end of the blót can begin. The meat of the slaughtered beasts is ready, the long fires are roaring and there is plenty of mead to go around.
Let the celebrations begin!
About time!
Your guests think better of you for a year.\nYou move inside the great hall...
The feast is over, and with it the blót. Nine winters must pass before you hold the next one, but as your vassals ride home most seem to agree it was well worth the journey.

The feast is over, and with it the blót. Nine winters must pass before [From.GetTitledFirstName] holds the next one, but as you and the other vassals ride home most seem to agree it was well worth the journey.
Until next time!
The mead and the spirits at the feast have got the better of you. You tried to be strong this time, and you did your best to keep away, but the pull was just too great...
*hic* Letsch drrink s-schome morr...

Your mouth waters as the servants set down tray after tray of food, and while the other guests talk, the only sounds from your corner are grunts and belches as you stuff yourself. A sudden sickness takes you and you hurry for the door, but only make it as far as the lap of [rites_feast_partner.GetTitledFirstName]...
UUAARGGHHHH...
Is sick in your lap.

Scraps of food and clean-picked bones fly from the direction of [From.GetTitledFirstName] as [From.GetSheHe] stuffs [From.GetHerselfHimself] with everything on the table. Suddenly [From.GetHerHis] face turns a strange shade of green, and [From.GetSheHe] rushes for the door but only makes it as far as your seat before emptying [From.GetHerHis] stomach into your lap...
Those were my best trousers!

As you enjoy the feast, you are struck by the warmth and kindness of those around you. In fact, it is getting just a little too warm. You strip off your clothes and leap onto the table. "Help, I'm on fire!" you scream at the top of your lungs, waving your arms while the other guests stare.
Put me out, put me out!

One of the servants pouring the mead has been eyeing you since you arrived, and now, fortified with drink, you pull the servant down beside you and the two of you give in to passion right there on the bench. Only when the hall falls silent does it dawn on you that every guest is watching...
Oops...
[Root.Spouse.GetFirstName] will not be happy about this...

You have been seated next to [rites_feast_partner.GetTitledFirstName] for the whole feast, and you have found [rites_feast_partner.GetHerHim] a most agreeable companion. You seem to have much in common.

You have been seated next to [rites_feast_culprit.GetTitledFirstName] for the whole feast, and you have found [rites_feast_culprit.GetHerHim] a most agreeable companion. You seem to have much in common.
It would seem I have a new friend.
You and your new friend think better of each other.

Your mind wanders as you sit at the feast, when suddenly you lock eyes with [rites_feast_partner.GetTitledFirstName]. Something in [rites_feast_partner.GetHerHis] gaze reaches into your heart, and when [rites_feast_partner.GetSheHe] steps outside for some fresh air, you quickly excuse yourself and follow.

Your mind wanders as you sit at the feast, when suddenly you lock eyes with [rites_feast_culprit.GetTitledFirstName]. Something in [rites_feast_culprit.GetHerHis] gaze reaches into your heart, and when you step outside for some fresh air, [rites_feast_culprit.GetSheHe] soon follows.

You lock eyes with [rites_feast_partner.GetTitledFirstName] across the hall, and when [rites_feast_partner.GetSheHe] steps outside you follow. You are locked in each other's arms when another guest stumbles out of the hall, sees you, and rushes back inside to tell everyone.

You lock eyes with [rites_feast_culprit.GetTitledFirstName] across the hall, and when you step outside [rites_feast_culprit.GetSheHe] follows. You are locked in each other's arms when another guest stumbles out of the hall, sees you, and rushes back inside to tell everyone.
I thought I was the only one...
It... it's not what it looks like!
The whole hall sees it.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has been drinking ever more since the feast began and can no longer stand. Surrounded by empty horns and singing at the top of [From.GetHerHis] lungs, [From.GetSheHe] lies sprawled on the table among the food.

Scraps of food and clean-picked bones fly from the direction of [From.GetTitledFirstName] as [From.GetSheHe] stuffs [From.GetHerselfHimself]. Suddenly [From.GetHerHis] face turns green, and [From.GetSheHe] rushes for the door but only makes it as far as [rites_feast_partner.GetTitledFirstName] before emptying [From.GetHerHis] stomach into poor [rites_feast_partner.GetFirstName]'s lap...

You are enjoying the feast when a shrill scream from the far end of the hall draws your eye. Stark naked, [From.GetTitledFirstName] is running up and down the table waving [From.GetHerHis] arms and screaming that [From.GetSheHe] is on fire. You groan and bury your face in your hands.

You are talking with another guest when cries of passion cut through the noise of the hall. On a bench in full view of everyone, [From.GetTitledFirstName] is coupling with one of the servants pouring the mead. Only when the hall falls silent do they seem to remember where they are.

With the hall spinning from all the mead, you stumble outside to relieve yourself and find [rites_feast_culprit.GetTitledFirstName] and [rites_feast_partner.GetTitledFirstName] locked in a passionate embrace. They spring apart the moment they see you.
I think [From.GetSheHe] has had enough.
*hic* I k-know thisch schong!
That could have been me...
That lunatic...
So [From.GetSheHe] is! And... and so am I! AAAHHH!
By [This.Religion.GetRandomGodNameCap]...
Haha, you old dog! Nicely done!
No! [From.GetFirstName], what have you done?!
By [This.Religion.GetRandomGodNameCap]! You... you two were...!
Oh, don't mind me. Carry on, friends.

Invitations have gone out to your vassals to join you in welcoming Dazh and the coming of spring. You mean to make this year's festival a special one, remembered by gods and men for many years to come.
Let us begin preparations.
Invitation to the festival of Dazh is sent.

Your liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName], has invited you to join [From.GetHerHim] in welcoming Dazh, the sun god, as the snows melt from the oblast. There will be fires, songs and a great feast to herald the coming of spring.
I will be there.
I will have nothing to do with that nonsense!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has declined your invitation to the festival! It seems [From.GetSheHe] has no faith in Dazh, Tor, Ursun and the other gods of Kislev, and follows some foreign cult instead.
A foolish mistake.

Your vassals have arrived, and the time has come to welcome Dazh and the spring. As tradition demands, one of them will be chosen to be paraded through the streets as Dazh himself, the fire-giver, in a golden chariot. Who shall it be?

At last the time has come to welcome Dazh and the spring. As tradition demands, one of the guests will be chosen to be paraded through the streets as Dazh himself, the fire-giver, in a golden chariot. Who shall it be?
Let us decide.
I hope it is me!

After much deliberation, you have been chosen to ride as Dazh this year! You are dressed in red and gold and a crown of golden straw is set on your head. Holding high a torch for the sun, you ride through the streets in a gilded chariot drawn by oxen, while a roaring crowd throws spring flowers and follows close behind.
All hail Dazh, the fire-giver!
I feel a right fool.

It has been decided that [From.GetTitledFirstName] will ride as Dazh this year! [From.GetSheHeCap] is dressed in red and gold, with a crown of golden straw on [From.GetHerHis] head. Holding high a torch for the sun, [From.GetFirstName] rides through the streets in a gilded chariot drawn by oxen, while a roaring crowd throws spring flowers and follows close behind.
All hail Dazh, the fire-giver!
Look at that fool.

As no fitting guest is at hand, it falls to you to ride as Dazh this year. You are dressed in red and gold and a crown of golden straw is set on your head. Holding high a torch for the sun, you ride through the streets in a gilded chariot drawn by oxen, while a roaring crowd throws spring flowers and follows close behind.
As the songs and fires die down outside, you and your vassals gather for the great feast your servants have prepared!
As the songs and fires die down outside, you gather with your liege and [From.GetHerHis] other vassals for the great feast [From.GetSheHe] has had prepared!
Let us drink together!
You have welcomed Dazh for another year, and your vassals are riding home. Most seem to agree that the festival was well worth the journey.
You have welcomed Dazh for another year, and the feast is over. You and the other vassals ride home agreeing that the festival was well worth the journey.
Blót Bowl
The bowl that caught the blood of the blót, with the bundle of twigs that sprinkled it on the idols and the faithful. Dark stains no scrubbing will lift ring its inside.

As your warriors come back from looting the holding, one of them hands you an axe with a strange purple sheen. Someone has carved a cross and the rune for two into its haft. You weigh it in your hand, and it feels better than any axe you have ever held. You toss your old axe aside.
I feel stronger.
This unnatural thing must be destroyed!

Among the loot your warriors carried out of the holding is a strange chest of some unknown metal. No blade, hammer or fire has been able to force it open, and what is inside remains a mystery. It has been brought to you.
One day that chest will be opened. Mark my words.
While looting the holding one of your warriors found a strange key of some unknown metal. As you turn it over in your hands, the metal reminds you of the chest you carried off years ago. Could it be?

While looting the holding one of your warriors found a strange key of some unknown metal. You have only seen such metal once before: the chest that has been handed down in your family and gathers dust in a corner of your hall. Could this be its key?
Let us see if it fits!

The key turns in the lock, and with trembling hands you lift the lid. The chest is full of ancient gold coins stamped with the faces of the long-dead priest-kings of Nehekhara and the strange picture-writing of the south.
A small fortune!

The key turns in the lock, and with trembling hands you lift the lid. Inside are only a few brittle scrolls, and they crumble into dust the moment you touch them. Whatever was written on them is lost for ever.
Just my luck.

The key turns in the lock, and with trembling hands you lift the lid. The chest is full of worthless baubles and trinkets. There is not a speck of gold, though a trader might give you a few coins for the lot.
Better than nothing, I suppose.

The key turns in the lock, and you lift the lid. There is nothing inside but a fine grey dust. As you run your fingers through it, pale lights begin to flicker in the room and the air turns as cold as a tomb. You squeeze your eyes shut as the first spectres take shape. You hear your guards screaming, and when you open your eyes again the spirits are gone... and so are your guards, but for a few heaps of ash.
This... this chest needs to be buried...

The raiding and looting done in your name have earned you a fearsome reputation. All along the coasts of the Old World, mothers tucking in their children warn them that if they misbehave, the terrible [Root.GetFirstName] will come ashore with [Root.GetHerHis] cursed warriors and eat them.
I like the sound of that!
Few alive are more feared than you. Where other Norscan reavers merely raid, you burn whole towns and castles, and leave no one alive but one to carry the tale of [Root.GetFirstName] the Ravager.
There is yet more work to be done.

You have taken whatever you want wherever the wild waves beat on rock or sand. No [Root.GetManWoman] sails a ship better, no [Root.GetManWoman] fights harder, and none is more feared. The other chieftains of Norsca bend the knee: you are a Norscan Warlord.
I do not sow.
The treasure your fleet has brought home has set the markets of [Root.Capital.GetName] buzzing, and more warriors hungry for gold are coming to your hall every day.
the wolf-spirit of Ulric
the bear-rage of Ursun
the fury of Grimnir
the howling rage of the northern gods

As the enemy line draws near, something wakes in you that you have never felt before: [Root.GetBerserkerSpirit]. Your blood roars in your ears, you bite down on the rim of your shield until the wood splinters, and with a howl that is not your own you hurl yourself alone into the enemy ranks. The cowards break and run at the sight of you, and your axe has no mercy for them.
Must... kill... more...

Shaking with the rage, you cleave the skull of yet another foe and turn to look for the next. Only then do you notice that your leg will not carry you: a spear has gone clean through it, and the bone beneath is shattered.
Only a flesh wound...
Shaking with the rage, you cleave the skull of yet another foe and turn to look for the next. Only then do you notice the long arrow standing out of your thigh, and the blood running into your boot.
Only a flesh wound...

The rage has carried you deep into the enemy ranks, and your own warriors are far behind. An arrow bites into your shoulder and two more into your chest. You throw your shield aside, take your axe in both hands and split one more skull before you fall to your knees. Then they are on you like a pack of dogs.
It is a good day to die...

Your sight turns red and [Root.GetBerserkerSpirit] takes you. You charge without a thought for your own skin, and while your companions struggle to keep up, your axe cuts a wide swath through the enemy. When the dust settles they find you standing over a heap of the slain, still snarling.
*a long, guttural howl*

You have been cheated of a glorious death in battle, and now the years have caught up with you. When the rage comes, your heart pounds until you cannot breathe, and your arms are heavy before the fight has well begun. The rage is for the young.
Perhaps it is.

[berserk_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] has been droning on at you for an hour about some trifle or other, and the rage is rising. You bite down hard on the edge of the table and taste blood and splinters. Froth gathers at the corners of your mouth, and your sight is starting to turn red...
Gggh... m-must... control... r-rage...
You may lose control.
You may hold the rage back.

When your servants burst in to see what the noise is, [berserk_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] stumbles past them with torn clothes, a mouth short of several teeth and a face swelling purple, and runs as if a bear were after [berserk_courtier.GetHerHim]. You sit among the wreckage, panting, waiting for the red to leave your eyes.
I probably should not have done that...

You bite a great chunk out of the table and spit it out while [berserk_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] goes on and on. With every scrap of your will you turn the rage away from [berserk_courtier.GetHerHim] and onto the table, and you hew it into firewood with your axe. As you lie panting in the splinters, [berserk_courtier.GetFirstName] finally stops to ask if you are feeling well, my [Root.GetTitle].
Yes... yes. I just need a moment.
the Blood God's fury

As the enemy draws near, you feel Khorne's gaze fall upon you. A blood-lust you cannot master swells in your chest, red-hot, and with a howl you raise your weapon and charge alone into the enemy ranks.
